title: The subjunctive after value judgments: what matters

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the subjunctive after value judgments from A2 Unit 27: *es importante que*, *es necesario que*, *es injusto que* + present subjunctive. Historians use it to say what matters when a country builds an identity.

sections.title: Value judgment + que + subjunctive
rows: Es importante que se estudie la vida real.
Es necesario que un país explique su pasado.
Es injusto que se olvide a las personas.

items.spanish: Es importante que se estudien los símbolos de la nación.
items.english: It is important that the symbols of the nation are studied.

items.spanish: Es necesario que el país explique bien su pasado.
items.english: It is necessary that the country explains its past well.

items.spanish: Es injusto que se olvide a las comunidades indígenas.
items.english: It is unfair that the indigenous communities are forgotten.

items.spanish: Es importante que los ciudadanos conozcan su historia.
items.english: It is important that citizens know their history.

sections.content: After *es importante / necesario / injusto que* use the present subjunctive (*estudie*, *explique*, *olvide*), not the indicative. A plain fact keeps the indicative: *Los símbolos dan orgullo*. In this unit the judgments are present-day opinions that historians give, so we use the present tense.
